title: NIAID dataset properties
description: The properties NIAID Data Discovery Portal records add to a CDIF dataset (composed with cdifCore and cdifDiscovery by the cdifNIAID profile; this module does NOT re-embed them). nde: terms are NIAID's (https://discovery.biothings.io/ns/nde/), bios: terms Bioschemas' (from the bioschemasSample block), and cdifniaid: terms the ones the portal uses that neither vocabulary declares. The properties NIAID adds to a DefinedTerm, a MonetaryGrant, a cited work, a Place and a DataCatalog are defined by the niaidDefinedTerm, niaidMonetaryGrant, niaidCreativeWork, niaidPlace and niaidDataCatalog blocks, which require those types. Every property accepts one value or an array, because framing collapses a one-element array to its value.

items.title: CDIF Concept-or-Term-or-String
items.description: Shared shape for a CDIF property that carries either a controlled-vocabulary value or a bare string label. Wraps cdifConceptOrTerm (SKOS-concept @id-ref, schema:DefinedTerm, or inline cdif:Concept) with a plain-string alternative used for legacy or single-word labels not yet bound to a vocabulary.

anyOf.description: A SKOS concept identified by URI, a schema:DefinedTerm, or an inline cdif:Concept. Shared shape used wherever a CDIF property carries either a controlled-vocabulary reference or an inline concept definition.
reference to a skos concept for the data type

schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known. A list when there are several; a single label may be a plain string, as JSON-LD framing writes a one-item list.

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

schema:affiliation.description: if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

schema:contactPoint.description: An email address or a contact web page (a form, an issue tracker), or both; at least one is required. Schema.org also allows telephone and postal contacts. A URL-only contact is ordinary in DCAT (a vcard:Kind with only vcard:hasURL), so requiring email made such records invalid.

NiaidDefinedTerm.title: NIAID defined term
NiaidDefinedTerm.description: A schema:DefinedTerm with NIAID's annotations. The NIAID Data Discovery Portal annotates every term it attaches to a dataset (species, infectious agents, health conditions, measurement techniques, variables): whether a curator checked it, the text it was matched from, who or what curated it, and for a taxon its common name. Across the portal's records these properties appear on DefinedTerms and nowhere else, so this block is an extension of that type and requires it.

allOf.description: A defined term, or a reference to one. It must name or identify the term.

nde:isCurated.description: Whether a curator checked the term against its source text.

nde:originalName.description: The text in the source record the term was matched from.

nde:curatedBy.description: Who or what produced or checked the annotation, often software (PubTator, GPT-4o-mini, the Biothings API).

cdifniaid:commonName.description: The common name of a taxon, e.g. Human for Homo sapiens.

Identifier.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

terms.description: NIAID's annotated terms; each must be a schema:DefinedTerm.

sample.description: A sample; nde:Sample is NIAID's subclass of the Bioschemas sample.

allOf.title: Bioschemas Sample properties
allOf.description: Properties of a biological sample from the Bioschemas Sample draft (https://bioschemas.org/), in the bios: namespace. A node using them is typed with bios:Sample beside its own type. Every property accepts one value or an array, because framing collapses a one-element array to its value. Ranges follow the Bioschemas draft where it gives one, and allow text where real records use text for a term.

bios:anatomicalStructure.description: The organ or tissue the sample was collected from.

bios:anatomicalSystem.description: The anatomical system the sample was collected from, e.g. circulatory, digestive, immune.

bios:associatedPhenotype.description: Defining characteristics expressed by the biological source of the sample.

bios:collectionMethod.description: Conditions and methods of acquisition of the sample.

bios:collector.description: The Person or Organization who collected the sample.

bios:dateCollected.description: The date the sample was collected.

bios:dateProcessed.description: The date the sample was processed or used in a method.

bios:developmentalStage.description: The age or developmental stage of the source when the sample was created, as a term or a quantity.

bios:environmentalSystem.description: The habitat or ecosystem where the sample was collected.

bios:experimentalPurpose.description: The planned or executed experimental procedures involving the sample.

bios:isControl.description: Whether the sample is used as a normal control.

bios:locationOfOrigin.description: The location from which the sample was originally collected.

bios:sampleAvailability.description: Whether the sample is available for reuse.

bios:sampleProcess.description: The processing technique applied to the sample.

bios:sampleState.description: The condition, composition or state of the sample, e.g. dried, frozen.

bios:sampleStorageTemperature.description: The temperature at which the sample is stored.

bios:sampleType.description: The type of sample, intentionally broad (cells, rock, sand).

bios:sex.description: The biological sex of the individual the sample was obtained from.

bios:studyID.description: The identifier of the study the sample belongs to.

bios:studyTitle.description: The title of the study the sample belongs to.

bios:project.description: The project the sample belongs to.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

quantity.description: A schema:QuantitativeValue; a range uses minValue and maxValue.

anyOf.description: A defined term, or a reference to one. It must name or identify the term.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).
